general_background.title: Making a soluble cadmium feed
general_background.summary: A carboxylic acid such as oleic acid can convert cadmium oxide into cadmium carboxylate in the flask. Changing this soluble feed and the free acid changes cadmium availability during nucleation and growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Formation of High-Quality CdTe, CdSe, and CdS Nanocrystals Using CdO as Precursor

general_background.title: Octadecene is not always inert
general_background.summary: Octadecene provides a weakly coordinating medium for hot solution growth, leaving the ligands more freedom to control surface binding. It can also polymerize under growth conditions, leaving an alkene-derived residue that is difficult to separate from hydrophobic nanocrystals.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: The Trouble with ODE: Polymerization during Nanocrystal Synthesis

general_background.title: A thiol can both supply sulfur and bind the surface
general_background.summary: In metal-sulfide routes that use an alkanethiol as the sulfur feed, metal–thiolate chemistry can supply sulfur to the growing lattice. Thiol or thiolate species can also bind at the particle surface, so sulfur delivery and surface capping may be linked.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Selective Nanocrystal Synthesis and Calculated Electronic Structure of All Four Phases of Copper–Antimony–Sulfide

general_background.title: Oleate and the nanocrystal surface
general_background.summary: Bound oleate can stabilize dispersed metal chalcogenide nanocrystals, and not all surface carboxylate need occupy the same binding environment. Displacing metal carboxylate from the surface can change surface stoichiometry as well as colloidal stability.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
